## Overview Fix a duplicate-cleanup assertion when NIXL TTL eviction races with another handshake lookup, and prevent old teardown from deleting state belonging to a new connection. Reuse `_handshake_lock` to serialize eviction, native teardown, handshake publication, and activity updates. Related: #56317, #59877, #62571, #59957. #56317 protects the agent-map pop but not the whole cleanup lifecycle. #59877 addresses native agent thread safety, which does not make transitions across multiple Python state collections atomic. #63144 handles agent recreation across sleep/wake; #62571 handles deferred notifications. These address different mechanisms. This PR does not include push cancellation, LMCache, model, or scheduler changes. ## Claims - Concurrent TTL scans do not assert because another thread has already removed the same engine. - Cleanup is idempotent, and reconnection state is not published before old native teardown finishes. - Preserve in-flight transfer protection and upstream draft TP mapping cleanup. - No claim of fixing all NIXL/native/shutdown races, improving throughput, or eliminating performance overhead. ## Validation Baseline: `3e75ccba298d0c7f045f35c39078cec74184b799`. The same final regression tests were run against both runtimes. | Check | Baseline | Patched | |---|---|---| | Repeated/concurrent cleanup regressions using normal worker construction | 3 failed with cleanup assertions | 3 passed | | Related lifecycle, TTL, handshake, and peer-replacement tests | Full subset not run | 93 passed, including the 3 new cases | | Existing push unit tests | Full module not run | 93 passed | | Native NIXL/UCX probe with controlled concurrent lookups | Assertions in 10/10 rounds | No errors in 100 rounds | | Native READ content verification after reconnection | 10/10; this does not negate the thread failures | 100/100 | | Real GPU OpenAI PD requests, OPT-125M | 48/48 outputs match | 48/48 outputs match | | Of those, requests after idle periods exceeding TTL | 8 rounds × 4 requests passed | 8 rounds × 4 requests passed | ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k ttl_cleanup -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k 'ttl or PeerReplacement or heartbeated or inflight_transfer or handshake' -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py -q ``` Unit-test environment: CPU/Gloo, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, NIXL 1.5.0, pytest 9.1.1. Unit tests and the native probe load the complete baseline/patched Python sources through `PYTHONPATH`, reusing a fixed native image; neither test compiles or invokes GPU kernels. The isolated runner supplies CPU/Gloo fixtures and reads the public OPT-125M config offline without loading weights. The new CPU CI job explicitly selects the three regressions; selection was checked with collect-only. Hosted execution of that job was not part of local validation. The native probe does not mock NIXL resource operations: it registers DRAM, creates/releases descriptors, removes/reconnects agents, and verifies the resulting UCX READ byte for byte. It uses lightweight worker-state initialization and in-process metadata exchange, with events controlling the interleaving at native removal. It is not a full worker startup, ZMQ handshake, GPU inference, or RDMA test. Its injected barrier makes its timings unsuitable as performance evidence. ### Serving validation and code checks Real OPT-125M weights, revision `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`; two isolated B300 GPU processes, TP1 prefill + TP1 decode, `NixlPushConnector`, `engine_ttl=2s`, eager execution, FP16. The client passes the prefill response's KV metadata to decode with the same request ID. Each result must exactly match standalone greedy inference and report `completion_tokens=16`. Each version passed 16 consecutive requests and eight rounds of four concurrent requests separated by three-second idle periods: 48 requests total. Prefill logs recorded eight actual TTL evictions per version. Decode's external KV transfer metrics confirmed that requests used transferred KV. The GPU extensions came from the existing image; the complete Python sources came from the baseline/patched checkout. Transfers used same-node UCX TCP/CUDA IPC, not cross-node RDMA. **The baseline also passed this natural serving workload; this is not a serving-level red/green reproduction of the race.** Integration scripts and logs were retained. Upstream `disaggregated.yaml` currently disables NIXL GPU jobs; this PR does not re-enable that group. Large-model cross-node TPS and production tail latency remain unmeasured. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and CI test tethering: ```bash pre-commit run --from-ref 3e75ccba298d0c7f045f35c39078cec74184b799 --to-ref HEAD ``` A separate native overhead probe without an injected barrier completed 30 rounds per version without errors. Median hot lookup time was approximately 0.621 → 0.852 μs. This ran on shared CPUs without a model and does not establish production performance parity.
Before/after regression output The same test file was run with the baseline and patched runtime. The isolated runner additionally used `--confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -p no:cacheprovider -p ttl_fixture_plugin --timeout=20`. The fixture plugin supplies the existing CPU/Gloo initialization; only the public OPT config is read. ```text # Before (abbreviated) AssertionError: assert engine_id in self._remote_agents FAILED ...::test_ttl_cleanup_is_idempotent FAILED ...::test_ttl_cleanup_concurrent_lookup[evict] FAILED ...::test_ttl_cleanup_concurrent_lookup[handshake] 3 failed # After 3 passed ```
## Details A production decode worker exited along this path (sanitized call stack): ```text start_load_kv _send_heartbeats _ensure_handshake _evict_stale_engines _cleanup_remote_engine assert engine_id in self._remote_agents AssertionError ``` In push mode, the engine thread reaches `_ensure_handshake` through heartbeats, while the writer thread reaches it through `_send_registration_to_p`. A possible interleaving is: 1. Thread A finds an expired peer, pops its remote agent, and starts native teardown. 2. The agent is gone, but its activity timestamp has not yet been removed. 3. Thread B performs another handshake lookup/TTL scan, selects the same peer, and asserts during cleanup. The existing RLock now serializes this lifecycle; repeated cleanup is harmless, and eviction is deferred while handshakes are pending. The production stack matches the controlled reproduction, but the available logs cannot uniquely establish the incident's exact thread interleaving. The tradeoff is that lookups using the same lock wait during native teardown, and pending handshakes delay TTL reclamation. No new lock or protocol is introduced, and model computation is unchanged. Production tail latency under frequent reconnections remains unquantified. AI assistance was used for implementation adaptation, regression tests, native reproduction, and documentation. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing lock, limits scope to NIXL lifecycle management, and documents the wider critical section's tradeoff. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** The submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line and running relevant tests. CPU regressions, the native probe, and real GPU PD validation passed; coverage limitations are disclosed above. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Preserves related behavior; formatting, type, and diff checks pass. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes the failure, reproduction, validation scope, and related upstream work.
Controlled native NIXL reproducer (CPU DRAM / UCX, not a GPU inference benchmark) ```python """Real vLLM lifecycle + NIXL/UCX DRAM probe, with controlled thread timing. No model, GPU, RDMA, or PD frontend. The pause forces a legal race window; agent registration, descriptors, removal, reconnection and READ are native. Handshake metadata is supplied in-process instead of through the wire protocol. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, TimeoutError import hashlib import inspect import json import threading import time import traceback import uuid from pathlib import Path from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np from nixl._api import nixl_agent, nixl_agent_config from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_worker import NixlBaseConnectorWorker parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument('--rounds', type=int, default=10) args = parser.parse_args() module_path = Path(inspect.getfile(NixlBaseConnectorWorker)) print(json.dumps({'source': str(module_path), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(module_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), 'rounds': args.rounds}), flush=True) class Wrapper: def __init__(self, agent): self.agent = agent self.entered = threading.Event() self.release = threading.Event() self.pause = False self.removes = 0 self.releases = 0 def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(self.agent, name) def remove_remote_agent(self, name): if self.pause: self.entered.set() if not self.release.wait(5): raise TimeoutError('teardown barrier timed out') self.agent.remove_remote_agent(name) self.removes += 1 def release_dlist_handle(self, handle): self.agent.release_dlist_handle(handle) self.releases += 1 results = [] for iteration in range(args.rounds): token = uuid.uuid4().hex local = nixl_agent('local-' + token, nixl_agent_config(backends=['UCX'])) peer = nixl_agent('peer-' + token, nixl_agent_config(backends=['UCX'])) src = np.full(4096, (iteration % 251) + 1, dtype=np.uint8) dst = np.zeros_like(src) local_reg = local.register_memory([(dst.ctypes.data, dst.nbytes, 0, '')], 'DRAM') peer_reg = peer.register_memory([(src.ctypes.data, src.nbytes, 0, '')], 'DRAM') peer_md = peer.get_agent_metadata() wrapper = Wrapper(local) w = object.__new__(NixlBaseConnectorWorker) w.shutdown = lambda: None # Probe explicitly owns/tears down native resources. w.nixl_wrapper = wrapper w._handshake_lock = threading.RLock() w._handshake_futures = {} w._engine_ttl = 1 w._engine_last_active = {} w._engine_clock_offset = {} w._remote_agents = {} w._engine_by_address = {} w._failed_remote_engines = set() w._invalid_remote_engines = set() w._recving_transfers = {} w._recving_metadata = {} w.transfer_topo = None for field in ('dst_xfer_side_handles', 'kv_caches_base_addr', 'dst_num_blocks', 'dst_region_num_blocks', 'dst_region_group_ids', 'dst_uses_region_group_mapping', 'dst_region_mem_types', 'tp_mappings', 'draft_tp_mappings'): setattr(w, field, {}) handshake_errors = [] w._log_failure = lambda **kw: handshake_errors.append(str(kw)) w.xfer_stats = SimpleNamespace(record_failed_handshake=lambda: None) w._handshake_initiation_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(1) def handshake(host, port, tp, eid, *rest): name = local.add_remote_agent(peer_md) handle = local.prep_xfer_dlist(name, [(src.ctypes.data, src.nbytes, 0)], 'DRAM') w.dst_xfer_side_handles[eid] = {0: handle} return {(0, 0): name}, 0.0 w._nixl_handshake = handshake agents, _ = handshake('localhost', 1234, 1, 'peer') w._remote_agents['peer'] = agents w._engine_last_active['peer'] = time.perf_counter() - 10 wrapper.pause = True errors = [] timings = [] def lookup(): start = time.perf_counter() try: future = w._ensure_handshake('peer', 'localhost', 1234, 1) if future is not None: future.result(timeout=5) except Exception: errors.append(traceback.format_exc()) finally: timings.append(time.perf_counter() - start) with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool: a = pool.submit(lookup) assert wrapper.entered.wait(5), 'did not reach real native teardown' second_started = threading.Event() def second_lookup(): second_started.set() lookup() b = pool.submit(second_lookup) assert second_started.wait(5) try: b.result(timeout=0.02) except TimeoutError: pass # Correctly locked lookup waits for native teardown. wrapper.release.set() a.result(timeout=5) b.result(timeout=5) wrapper.pause = False w._handshake_initiation_executor.shutdown(wait=True) assert not handshake_errors, handshake_errors assert 'peer' in w._remote_agents local_handle = local.prep_xfer_dlist('', [(dst.ctypes.data, dst.nbytes, 0)], 'DRAM') h = local.make_prepped_xfer('READ', local_handle, [0], w.dst_xfer_side_handles['peer'][0], [0]) state = local.transfer(h) deadline = time.monotonic() + 5 while state not in ('DONE', 'ERR') and time.monotonic() < deadline: state = local.check_xfer_state(h) assert state == 'DONE', state local.release_xfer_handle(h) assert np.array_equal(src, dst), 'real post-reconnect READ corrupted data' local.release_dlist_handle(local_handle) w._cleanup_remote_engine('peer', log_eviction=False) local.deregister_memory(local_reg) peer.deregister_memory(peer_reg) row = {'round': iteration, 'errors': errors, 'lookup_seconds': timings, 'native_removes': wrapper.removes, 'native_descriptor_releases': wrapper.releases, 'post_reconnect_read_ok': True} results.append(row) print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) del w, wrapper, local, peer print(json.dumps({'summary': True, 'rounds': len(results), 'failed_rounds': sum(bool(r['errors']) for r in results), 'read_ok': sum(r['post_reconnect_read_ok'] for r in results)}), flush=True) ``` Run `UCX_TLS=tcp,self UCX_NET_DEVICES=lo UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024 .venv/bin/python native_lifecycle_probe.py --rounds 10` against the baseline and patched Python sources. Inspect the final `failed_rounds`, not just the exit code: the script catches thread exceptions so it can continue verifying post-reconnection READs.

Correctly locked lookup waits for native teardown. wrapper.release.set() a.result(timeout=5) b.result(timeout=5) wrapper.pause = False w._handshake_initiation_executor.shutdown(wait=True) assert not handshake_errors, handshake_errors assert 'peer' in w._remote_agents local_handle = local.prep_xfer_dlist('', [(dst.ctypes.data, dst.nbytes, 0)], 'DRAM') h = local.make_prepped_xfer('READ', local_handle, [0], w.dst_xfer_side_handles['peer'][0], [0]) state = local.transfer(h) deadline = time.monotonic() + 5 while state not in ('DONE', 'ERR') and time.monotonic() < deadline: state = local.check_xfer_state(h) assert state == 'DONE', state local.release_xfer_handle(h) assert np.array_equal(src, dst), 'real post-reconnect READ corrupted data' local.release_dlist_handle(local_handle) w._cleanup_remote_engine('peer', log_eviction=False) local.deregister_memory(local_reg) peer.deregister_memory(peer_reg) row = {'round': iteration, 'errors': errors, 'lookup_seconds': timings, 'native_removes': wrapper.removes, 'native_descriptor_releases': wrapper.releases, 'post_reconnect_read_ok': True} results.append(row) print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) del w, wrapper, local, peer print(json.dumps({'summary': True, 'rounds': len(results), 'failed_rounds': sum(bool(r['errors']) for r in results), 'read_ok': sum(r['post_reconnect_read_ok'] for r in results)}), flush=True) ``` Run `UCX_TLS=tcp,self UCX_NET_DEVICES=lo UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024 .venv/bin/python native_lifecycle_probe.py --rounds 10` against the baseline and patched Python sources. Inspect the final `failed_rounds`, not just the exit code: the script catches thread exceptions so it can continue verifying post-reconnection READs.

+def lifecycle_worker(default_vllm_config, dist_init):

+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("second_operation", ["evict", "handshake"])
+def test_ttl_cleanup_concurrent_lookup(lifecycle_worker, second_operation):
+    """A teardown cannot invalidate another lookup or its new descriptors."""
+    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, TimeoutError
+
+    worker = lifecycle_worker
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
+    while (
+        time.perf_counter() - worker._engine_last_active["remote_engine"]
+        <= worker._engine_ttl
+    ):
+        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "peer did not expire"
+        threading.Event().wait(0.001)
+
+    removing = threading.Event()
+    release = threading.Event()
+    second_started = threading.Event()
+    native_remove = worker.nixl_wrapper.remove_remote_agent
+
+    def paused_remove(name):
+        removing.set()
+        assert release.wait(5), "test teardown barrier timed out"
+        return native_remove(name)
+
+    def second_lookup():

+        return worker._ensure_handshake("remote_engine", "localhost", 1234, 1)
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(worker.nixl_wrapper, "remove_remote_agent", paused_remove),
+        ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool,
+    ):
+        first = pool.submit(worker._evict_stale_engines)
+        try:
+            assert removing.wait(5)
+            second = pool.submit(second_lookup)
+            assert second_started.wait(5)
+            with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
+                second.result(timeout=0.1)
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+        first.result(timeout=5)
+        pending = second.result(timeout=5)
+        if pending is not None:
+            assert pending.result(timeout=5)[0]
+
+    pending = worker._ensure_handshake("remote_engine", "localhost", 1234, 1)
+    if pending is not None:
+        assert pending.result(timeout=5)[0]
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
+    while "remote_engine" not in worker._remote_agents:
+        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "reconnection was not published"
+        threading.Event().wait(0.001)
+    assert worker.dst_xfer_side_handles["remote_engine"]
